categories.main_business_segments: China Construction Bank Corporation (CCB) operates primarily in four main business segments: corporate banking, personal banking, funds and asset management, and other businesses including overseas operations. Corporate banking services include corporate loans, trade finance, cash management, investment banking, and international business. Personal banking covers personal loans, deposits, wealth management, credit cards, rural revitalization, housing leasing, and entrusted housing finance. Funds and asset management involve money market operations, asset management, interbank business, and custody services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: CCB leverages advanced technologies such as internet, big data, artificial intelligence, biometric identification, and cloud computing to enhance its financial services. It has developed a comprehensive digital ecosystem including AI-powered financial models, digital RMB applications, and intelligent customer service assistants. The bank has implemented a distributed core system transformation and maintains a high-performance computing platform ('CCB Cloud') with significant GPU resources. It also employs financial big data analytics and AI-driven risk management tools to optimize credit evaluation and operational efficiency.
categories.primary_customers_markets: CCB serves a vast customer base including 771 million individual customers and 11.68 million corporate clients. Its corporate clients span government agencies, financial institutions, private enterprises, and multinational corporations. The bank focuses on key sectors such as manufacturing, strategic emerging industries, green finance, rural and agricultural enterprises, and digital economy core industries. It also targets high-net-worth individuals through private banking and wealth management services, and supports small and micro enterprises and inclusive finance customers.
categories.geographic_coverage: CCB operates extensively across China with a network of 14,750 branches and subsidiaries, covering all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities. It has a significant presence in major economic regions including the Yangtze River Delta, Pearl River Delta, Bohai Rim, Central China, Western China, and Northeast China. Internationally, CCB has branches and subsidiaries in 28 countries and regions across six continents, including Hong Kong, Singapore, Europe, North America, Australia, and parts of Asia and Africa, with specialized subsidiaries in Russia, Europe, New Zealand, Indonesia, Malaysia, and the UK.
categories.supply_chain_position: CCB operates primarily as a downstream financial services provider within the financial supply chain, offering banking, credit, investment, and asset management services to both corporate and individual clients. It acts as a financial intermediary facilitating capital flow, credit provision, and payment settlement. Additionally, through its subsidiaries, it engages in insurance, leasing, trust, and investment activities, integrating vertically within the financial services ecosystem.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: CCB's strategic focus emphasizes high-quality development through innovation in five key financial areas: technology finance, green finance, inclusive finance, pension finance, and digital finance. It prioritizes building capabilities in serving national strategies, risk prevention, and international competition. The bank invests heavily in fintech, including AI and big data, developing financial large models and intelligent applications to enhance customer experience and operational efficiency. It also focuses on sustainable finance, digital RMB innovation, and expanding services for emerging industries and rural revitalization.
categories.revenue_model: CCB generates revenue primarily through net interest income from loans and deposits, fee and commission income from banking services such as wealth management, payment services, and investment banking. It also earns income from trading and investment securities, insurance premiums via subsidiaries, and asset management fees. The bank's diversified revenue streams include interest on loans, fees for advisory and custody services, trading gains, and income from financial product sales and digital financial services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: CCB is one of China's leading large commercial banks and ranks among the top global banks by market capitalization and brand value. It holds the 6th position globally among listed banks and is ranked 2nd in the 2024 Global Banking 1000 list by The Banker magazine. Its main competitors include other major Chinese state-owned banks such as Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), Agricultural Bank of China (ABC), and Bank of China (BOC). CCB positions itself as a technology-driven, sustainable, and customer-centric bank with strong capabilities in serving the real economy and national strategic initiatives.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of the end of 2024, CCB's total assets exceeded RMB 40.57 trillion, marking a 5.86% increase year-over-year. The bank achieved a net profit of RMB 336.28 billion, growing 1.15% compared to the previous year. Key financial ratios include a return on assets (ROA) of 0.85%, return on equity (ROE) of 10.69%, and a capital adequacy ratio of 19.69%. The bank maintains a low non-performing loan ratio of 1.34% and a provision coverage ratio of 233.60%. It serves a large customer base with over 7.7 billion individual accounts and 11.68 million corporate clients, supported by nearly 377,000 employees.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: CCB emphasizes its commitment to serving the real economy with high-quality, diversified financial services tailored to national strategic priorities. It differentiates itself through integrated financial solutions across corporate, personal, and asset management sectors, supported by advanced digital technologies and AI-driven services. The bank offers comprehensive support for emerging industries, green finance, rural revitalization, and pension finance, positioning itself as a sustainable and innovative financial institution. Its extensive branch network and digital platforms provide broad accessibility and personalized customer experiences, reinforcing its role as a trusted partner in China's economic development.
